passages.passage: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut dominated the session, raising a record $81.3 billion at $83/share and briefly hitting a $2 trillion market cap — before retreating nearly 9% from its opening high as the broader Nasdaq turned negative in choppy trade. The IPO ignited a global semiconductor and AI infrastructure rally in premarket, but that enthusiasm faded as macro concerns, a short-seller attack on AMD, and a cyberattack hitting JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard vendors weighed on sentiment. European markets closed broadly lower despite the AI excitement, while Asia saw sharp losses led by Taiwan's 4.6% plunge.

🔴 Taiwan / Semiconductors | Taiwan Weighted Index plunges 4.6% to six-month low; chip and PCB shares hit limit-down Market Impact: The sharp selloff — driven by AI spending doubts and TSMC tightening China chip restrictions — undercut the Anthropic-driven optimism and weighed on global semiconductor sentiment.

Anthropic's IPO is a watershed moment for AI market structure, but Thursday's price action delivered a cautionary message: even the world's largest IPO couldn't sustain a broad market rally. The Nasdaq's intraday reversal from +1% to negative, combined with AMD's sharp drop on China-linked scrutiny and Taiwan's 4.6% plunge, suggests the AI trade is bifurcating — pure-play AI infrastructure names (storage, networking, cybersecurity) are finding buyers, while the broader semiconductor complex remains vulnerable to geopolitical and regulatory headwinds. Record-negative dealer gamma, as flagged in session analysis, is amplifying moves in both directions, making this an unusually volatile tape.

all boats right now. - 🔴 AMD: Down 8-9% on Hunterbrook Capital short report flagging China export risks — China-exposed chip names face a new layer of regulatory overhang. - 🟢 PANW: Raised annual forecast and beat across the board — cybersecurity demand is accelerating, and the whole sector is trading on that signal. - 🔴 JPM/Visa/Mastercard: Third-party vendor cyberattack leaked customer data — financial sector cyber risk is real and ongoing, even when the core systems aren't breached. - 🔴 Taiwan TAIEX: -4.6% to a six-month low with chip/PCB names hitting limit-down — Asia's AI selloff is not over. - 🟢 Insmed (INSM): +16-18% on Sanofi acquisition report — biotech M&A is alive; rare disease assets command significant premiums. - 🟢 GTA VI / Sony: PlayStation captured ~75% of first-day GTA VI sales; Sony +3% — console hardware holders are the quiet winners of the gaming launch. - 🔴 Take-Two (TTWO): -2.7% on GTA VI launch day — classic "sell the news" after years of anticipation baked
